question: In 2005, a project to extend ski slopes severely compromised the integrity of site No IT2040044. The CJEU ruled against Italy in this case (C-304/05). As a compensatory measure, the ‘Tresero - Dosso del Vallon’ national nature reserve was then set up, with a ‘stricter legally binding statutory framework’ than the surrounding Natura 2000 sites.

A project is now under way to install artificial snow cannons on the ski slopes within the site and the reserve. It involves extensive earthworks, which will degrade the habitat and disturb species protected under Directives 92/43/EEC (Annex I) and 2009/147/EC (Annex I).

Because of this project, approved on the basis of the wrong kind of environmental impact assessment (EIA), and the earthworks involved, damage is thus once again being done to the site, as well as the reserve set up in response to the CJEU judgment. In view of the above: 1.

Is the Commission aware of the serious damage currently being done to site IT2040044 and the ‘Tresero - Dosso del Vallon’ nature reserve, set up as a compensatory measure adopted in response to the CJEU judgment (Case C-304/05)?
What action could be taken to guarantee and restore the integrity of the site and safeguard the effectiveness of the compensatory measure?
Will it will assess the outcome of EU Pilot 6730/14/ENVI, also in view of the unsuitable EIA that allowed the project to be carried out?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.5.2024) 1. In December 2023, the Commission received a letter on the project in question. The project was then subject to a petition discussed at the Committee on Petitions meeting1. The Commission is assessing the petition and will provide its reply in writing. 2. According to Article 6.

3 of the Habitats Directive (HD)2, any project not directly connected with or necessary to the management of the site but likely to have a significant effect thereon shall be subject to appropriate assessment of its implications for the site in view of the site's conservation objectives.
If compensatory measures from a previous project have already been implemented in the same site, they will be part of the baseline for the assessment under Article 6.3. According to Article 6.

4 of the HD, if, in spite of a negative assessment of the implications for the site and in the absence of alternative solutions, a project must nevertheless be carried out for imperative reasons of overriding public interest, the Member State shall take all compensatory measures necessary to ensure that the overall coherence of Natura 2000 is protected.

Italy has transposed the above-mentioned provisions in its legislation3 and has adopted national guidelines4 to improve their implementation. The Lombardy region has also adopted updated guidelines and procedures for the proper implementation of these provisions5.

Without prejudice to the Commission’s role as guardian of the Treaties, it is for the Italian competent authorities to apply the above rules and procedures to an individual case. 3. The Commission is currently assessing several complaints received in the framework of EU Pilot 6730/14, including the above-mentioned petition, and will decide in due course on the appropriate action to take6.
